column2: w379_L02.10: readers r/c; eye: 76.77: the 22.23 x/r shape, small; not the plain c of 375 L02 76.77 (outside the tile's candidates c, r as a label); which of c, r, or another sign?
w379_L03.12: readers j/f; eye: 46.47: short descender with a dot above, could be a short long-s or j; neither f nor j firm; which of f, j, or another sign?
x375_379.3: readers c/r; eye: 375 glyph a plain c (H); 379 glyph the small x/r shape (H): two firm, different readings -- a witness difference; which of c, r, or another sign?
x375_379.5: readers e/w; eye: both glyphs one shape (double bowl with a tail); e vs w is naming, neither firm (M); which of e, w, or another sign?
x375_379.8: readers s/j; eye: 375 long-s (H); 379 the short sign of w379_L03.12 (L); which of j, s, or another sign?
x375_379.17: readers x/c; eye: both glyphs the 64.65 curled sign (same class, M); x vs c naming not firm; which of c, x, or another sign?
x375_379.37: readers x/c; eye: both glyphs the 64.65 curled sign (M); x vs c naming not firm; which of c, x, or another sign?
x375_379.44: readers SYM/f; eye: 375 glyph an ink blot (illegible); 379 a short looped long-s; which of SYM, f, or another sign?
w379_L07.8 (46.47, both readers f, not a split tile): the eye sees a tall long-s without crossbar, the shape settled s at 375 L07.1 and unit 27; f or s?
the sign after 64.65 (375 L05/L07/L11, 379 L06/L08/L12): one curled sign throughout, named x on 375 and c on 379; is it x, c, or its own sign (distinct from the 22.23 x and the 76.77 plain c)?
